messages:
alana: Heads-up — Transitly reporting a surge of 504s / request_queue_timeout on hosted inference since ~09:40 UTC. P95 and p99 tail latency spiking. Customer traffic: concurrent clients ~350, avg batch size ~10-14, seq len ~1800-2200. They say errors: 504 gateway, and internal code 'REQ_QUEUE_TIMEOUT'.
ops-bot: [alert] hosted-gateway: high_request_queue_depth for tenant transitly detected (threshold 1200) :rotating_light:
devon: Thanks. Can you paste a sample request_id and a short trace? Any rollout or infra changes around that time?
alana: sample request id: r-20240315-9a7c5. No infra deploys in the window per deploy-bot. Customer says they ramped concurrency + increased client-side retries at 09:35.
alana: Paste from API gateway logs:
```
2024-03-15T09:41:02Z INFO request_id=r-20240315-9a7c5 tenant=transitly route=/v1/generate status=504 reason=REQ_QUEUE_TIMEOUT queue_len=1842 batch_id=cb-778
2024-03-15T09:41:02Z DEBUG kvcache.evictions=0 batcher.backlog=748 continuous-batcher.pending=132
2024-03-15T09:41:02Z WARN request_id=r-20240315-9a7c5 latency_ms=12034 p95_tail=true
```
ashok: Those numbers look like continuous-batcher backlog > default max_queue depth for hosted. Could be a combo of large seq len + simultaneous long requests -> KV cache spinup + slow dequeues. What's the current max_queue_depth on that pool?
devon: I'm checking runtime metrics now (admin):
```
> adminctl pool metrics --pool hosted-eu-g2
pool=hosted-eu-g2 queue_depth=1842 max_queue_depth=1024 running_batches=64 pending_batches=132 avg_batch_size=11
```
devon: Queue depth doubled past max (1842 > 1024). That's the direct cause of REQ_QUEUE_TIMEOUTs; gateway enforces early rejects when queue over threshold.
julia: Customer is on Dedicated-ish SLAs? Transitly on self-serve but pretty sensitive. They already opened a support ticket and asked for ETA.
ashok: Immediate mitigations: 1) temporary increase max_queue_depth on that pool to 4096 (risk: memory). 2) enable overflow-shedding policy so very-large seq requests get routed to lower-priority fallback. 3) ask customer to throttle concurrency / backoff retries.
devon: I can push a config bump for hosted-eu-g2: set MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH=4096 and enable overflow_shed=true. Will do a staged change to avoid OOMs.
alana: Can we also add a short-term autopurge for cold kvcache warmups? Those long seqs are expensive.
ashok: Yes — enable kvcache-warmup-throttle which defers non-critical prefix warming for 30s. Helps throughput.
devon: executing change now (rolling to 4 nodes at a time):
```
> infractl set-pool-config hosted-eu-g2 --max-queue-depth 4096 --overflow-shed true --kv-warmup-throttle 30s
Applying to 12 nodes... 2/12 updated
```
devon: Update: after first 4 nodes, queue depth on those nodes dropped ~40% (per-node queue redistributed). Global pool depth now 1260 and trending down.
ops-bot: [alert-resolve] hosted-gateway: high_request_queue_depth for tenant transitly resolved (current=890) :white_check_mark:
alana: Customer confirms error rate falling from 8% -> 0.8% over the last 10 min. They accepted temporary throttle guidance.
julia: I'll send a customer note: summary of root cause (ingress spike + large long-seq batches causing continuous-batcher backlog > configured queue depth), actions taken (increased queue limit, enabled overflow-shed, kvcache warmup throttle), and recommended client-side mitigations.
devon: Follow-ups for postmortem: - add better autoscale for pool queue depth - surface tenant-level circuit-breaker metrics in console - add a safety cap that rejects aggressively long sequences instead of allowing queue to inflate.
ashok: Also test: simulate a mix of long seqs + high concurrency in staging with continuous-batcher to validate new defaults (max_queue_depth=4096, kv-warmup-throttle).
\alana: Noting timeline and who did what for CS. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours and then close the incident if stable.
julia: Thanks all. Will sync with Transitly at 12:30 UTC and offer a follow-up call if they want deeper tuning. :+1:
